messages.task:
You are a financial-analysis assistant who can reason step-by-step and call external tools when needed.  All numeric evidence you require lives inside these tools – no numbers have been provided directly in this prompt.  Use the tools to look up data, transform it, and compute an answer that can be verified.

Scenario
A multinational packaging company reports its results by operating segment.  The Metal Beverage Packaging, Europe segment’s narrative explains how net sales changed over time:
• 2010 net sales fell compared with 2009, largely because of foreign-exchange headwinds, price/mix changes, and other factors.
• 2009 net sales also fell versus 2008, owing mainly to adverse currency translation, mitigated somewhat by commercial improvements.
The narrative asks us to quantify how the 2010 decrease compares with the 2009 decrease.

Available tools (call them as functions; inspect their docstrings for full signatures)
1. list_all_segments() – return every business-segment name.
2. get_segments_by_region(region_keyword) – filter segments by region.
3. get_net_sales_local(segment_name, year) – fetch a segment’s net-sales figure and its original reporting currency for the given fiscal year.
4. fx_rate_to_usd(currency, year) – return the historical FX rate (local units per 1 USD).
5. convert_to_usd(amount, currency, year) – convert any local amount into USD for the specified year.
6. compute_sales_change_usd(segment_name, start_year, end_year) – compute the change in net sales (in USD) between two years.
7. absolute_value(number) – numeric helper.
8. subtract_numbers(a, b) – numeric helper (a − b).
9. round_to_one_decimal(number) – round to one decimal place.
(Additional helper tools exist but may not be necessary.)

Question
“The segment sales decrease in 2010 was what percent of the decrease in 2009?”

Instructions
Devise a plan that chains the tools to arrive at the single numeric answer (with one decimal place). Think aloud, but output only the final answer (just the number) once you have finished reasoning.  If you need data, call the tools; do not hallucinate numbers.
